q-516.name: Question 1
q-516.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying the equation through by $5$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x-4}{5} & =4 \\ 5(\frac{3x-4}{5}) & =5\cdot 4 \\ \cancel{5}(\frac{3x-4}{\cancel{5}}) & =20 \\ 3x-4 & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-4 & =20 \\ 3x-4+4 & =20+4 \\ 3x & =24 \\ \frac{3x}{3} & =\frac{24}{3} \\ \frac{\cancel{3}x}{\cancel{3}} & =\frac{24}{3} \\ x & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

If 3x−45=4, then x=

3

EXPLANATION

First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying the equation through by 5: 3x−45=45(3x−45)=5⋅45(3x−45)=203x−4=20

Then, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles: 3x−4=203x−4+4=20+43x=243x3=2433x3=243x=8

q-175605.name: Question 2
q-175605.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying the equation through by $4$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{10-3x}{4} & =1 \\ 4(\frac{10-3x}{4}) & =4\cdot 1 \\ \cancel{4}(\frac{10-3x}{\cancel{4}}) & =4 \\ 10-3x & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}10-3x & =4 \\ 10-3x-10 & =4-10 \\ -3x & =-6 \\ \frac{-3x}{-3} & =\frac{-6}{-3} \\ \frac{\cancel{-3}x}{\cancel{-3}} & =\frac{6}{3} \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

q-101638.name: Question 3
q-101638.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying the equation through by $3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7w+10}{3} & =4w \\ 3(\frac{7w+10}{3}) & =3\cdot (4w) \\ \cancel{3}\cdot (\frac{7w+10}{\cancel{3}}) & =12w \\ 7w+10 & =12w\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}7w+10 & =12w \\ 7w+10-7w & =12w-7w \\ 10 & =5w \\ \frac{10}{5} & =\frac{5w}{5} \\ 2 & =w\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $w=2.$

q-44323.name: Question 4
q-44323.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying the equation through by $4$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7-2x}{4} & =3x \\ 4(\frac{7-2x}{4}) & =4\cdot 3x \\ \cancel{4}(\frac{7-2x}{\cancel{4}}) & =12x \\ 7-2x & =12x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}7-2x & =12x \\ 7-2x+2x & =12x+2x \\ 7 & =14x \\ 14x & =7 \\ \frac{14x}{14} & =\frac{7}{14} \\ \frac{\cancel{14}x}{\cancel{14}} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

q-44323.html:
Question 4
?

Solve the equation 7−2x4=3x.

a
x=724
b
x=4
c
x=2
d
x=710
e
x=12
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying the equation through by 4: 7−2x4=3x4(7−2x4)=4⋅3x4(7−2x4)=12x7−2x=12x

Then, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles: 7−2x=12x7−2x+2x=12x+2x7=14x14x=714x14=71414x14=12x=12

q-44322.name: Question 5
q-44322.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying the equation through by $4$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5y+12}{4} & =2y \\ 4(\frac{5y+12}{4}) & =4\cdot 2y \\ \cancel{4}(\frac{5y+12}{\cancel{4}}) & =8y \\ 5y+12 & =8y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}5y+12 & =8y \\ 5y+12-5y & =8y-5y \\ 12 & =3y \\ \frac{12}{3} & =\frac{3y}{3} \\ 4 & =\frac{\cancel{3}y}{\cancel{3}} \\ 4 & =y \\ y & =4\end{aligned}
$$

b

q-178530.name: Question 6
q-178530.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by $2.$ 
We must make sure that all of the terms on the left-hand side are multiplied by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5y-7 & =\frac{16-5y}{2} \\ 2(5y-7) & =2(\frac{16-5y}{2}) \\ 2\cdot 5y+2\cdot (-7) & =\cancel{2}(\frac{16-5y}{\cancel{2}}) \\ 10y-14 & =16-5y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}10y-14 & =16-5y \\ 10y-14+5y & =16-5y+5y \\ 15y-14 & =16 \\ 15y-14+14 & =16+14 \\ 15y & =30 \\ \frac{15y}{15} & =\frac{30}{15} \\ \frac{\cancel{15}y}{\cancel{15}} & =\frac{30}{15} \\ y & =2\end{aligned}
$$

q-171596.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3+m}{7} & =2m-7 \\ 7(\frac{3+m}{7}) & =7(2m-7) \\ \cancel{7}(\frac{3+m}{\cancel{7}}) & =14m-49 \\ 3+m & =14m-49\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}3+m & =14m-49 \\ 3+m-m & =14m-49-m \\ 3 & =13m-49 \\ 3+49 & =13m-49+49 \\ 52 & =13m \\ \frac{52}{13} & =\frac{13m}{13} \\ 4 & =\frac{\cancel{13}m}{\cancel{13}} \\ 4 & =m \\ m & =4\end{aligned}

q-101642.name: Question 8
q-101642.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying the equation through by $2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}3(2t-1) & =\frac{4t-3}{2} \\ 2\cdot (3(2t-1)) & =2(\frac{4t-3}{2}) \\ 6(2t-1) & =\cancel{2}(\frac{4t-3}{\cancel{2}}) \\ 12t-6 & =4t-3\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}12t-6 & =4t-3 \\ 12t-6-4t & =-3+4t-4t \\ 8t-6 & =-3 \\ 8t-6+6 & =-3+6 \\ 8t & =3 \\ \frac{8t}{8} & =\frac{3}{8} \\ t & =\frac{3}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

q-101643.name: Question 9
q-101643.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying the equation through by $3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2n-8}{3} & =-6(n+1) \\ 3\cdot (\frac{2n-8}{3}) & =3\cdot (-6(n+1)) \\ \cancel{3}\cdot (\frac{2n-8}{\cancel{3}}) & =-18(n+1) \\ 2n-8 & =-18n-18\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}2n-8 & =-18n-18 \\ 2n-8+18n & =-18n-18+18n \\ 20n-8 & =-18 \\ 20n-8+8 & =-18+8 \\ 20n & =-10 \\ \frac{20n}{20} & =\frac{-10}{20} \\ n & =-\frac{10}{20} \\ n & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
